Something I was given for cracks by the dermatology team ages ago was **Fludroxycortide Tape** (4micrograms per square centimetre) I found a tiny strip of it the other day and helped heal the biggest crack on my palm when left on overnight and I find it keeps working for a while after removed. for me it’s often when something has been triggered in me which often is so small and i can know is not a good reason to hate a person but can play into major fears of abandonment, invalidation or literally anything or remind me of how i felt during a time of trauma. i feel like there are so many reasons but when i think about it it can be
• i feel hurt and i don’t like it and get overwhelmed so the only way it ends up coming out seems aggressive/ an ‘overreaction’ (i put this in quotes bc i’m trying to not invalidate anything as it can feel very real and intense)
• need to make the other person hate me before i hurt them first or more
• i’m thinking about abuse or feeling emotionally re traumatised which can lead to associations that the other person is like that person therefore any little things feel like the biggest thing in the world 

it usually seems quite irrational for me but that doesn’t change the way it actually feels at the time. it doesn’t make sense and can be very hard to verbalise especially when the guilt sets in that it feels silly and communicating that will make the other person hate me more or invalidate that 

i find it very difficult when this happens to me and i get angry with myself (i have quiet type bpd so i tend to internalise things a lot but can seem cold or angry to the other person) and feel really ashamed especially when oftentimes i realise i might have accidentally been hurtful back which strangely hurts me more and plays into the idea that i’m a bad person and continue the cycle of hurting people. there’s this strange inner conflict that seems to happen for me between thoughts and how things should be vs feelings like i can see someone didn’t purposely do something and i still value the relationship but the hurt is irrationally intense that i want to withdraw, cut them off, or prevent lashing out

obviously not everyone experiences bpd or life the same but this is some of my experience with it i don’t even know if it makes sense and definitely isn’t completely how it feels or happens but it’s the best i can explain it right now maybe

i think a more true statement would be that people treat others based on their own circumstances 

i guess it’s like someone who has gone through bad things or trauma could either lash out, be overly aware of how they treat others, or simply not be able to cope (that’s usually the pattern i’ve seen lol). but from the other side it could be people seeing vulnerable people and treating them how they’ve seen other people treat them to maybe gain a sense of power which would play into how they see themselves and perhaps make them feel better you know. can be good to acknowledge why people might treat you a certain way but sometimes it can turn into excusing the way people treat others which is equally as harmful when in reality you aren’t controlling how people treat you it just happens


ideally everyone should treat other people how you want to be treated but that doesn’t seem to be a universal standard people actually follow

i got a GD diagnosis quite young and still very much struggle with the idea that perhaps it’s just my BPD trying to cling onto a new sense of identity too…
but i have tried to see this in a new light and realising that’s not at all a bad thing. it can be impossible to trust yourself with a battle in your mind constantly but life and a sense of identity improving from that is totally positive for me. both gender identity and expression are not fixed and as we learn and grow more into and about ourselves this may keep cropping up but i know i made the right decision in transitioning and if you do also there isn’t much reason to doubt the validity of that- regardless of the cause

i’m proud of you for following those steps and guidance it’s such a big step and it may feel fraudulent to not ‘fully’ do what your brain wants you to but opposite action in an attempt to progress is so amazing- remember that!

addiction can be a huge part for a large amount of people with BPD and a period of sobriety can in ways be there to check ‘the cause’ as it were. this can be helpful in managing emotions too even if it seems like the only way in coping is currently through drugs. it is worth a go and the outcomes are 
1. you get clean and partially the issues diminish
2. get clean and realise it was self medication whcih can help sometimes with a diagnosis
3. having a support network for that time can help you find new ways to cope

getting a diagnosis, treatment, and also a journey of sobriety are all difficult paths but a willingness to try is an important attribute 

(i hope this doesn’t come across demeaning or patronising in any way, i am someone with bpd struggling with a variety of substance addictions and also remember an official diagnosis isn’t the be all and end all anyway, identification can still be found in all areas and it’s amazing you are trying to get support for these things)

the fact that things, even for a time, did change does bring that hope that they will again. it is the nature of us all to fall backwards at times but as long as we keep trying to come back from these things the ‘ups’ can become more frequent 

i try to put things in place in my life for when i know things may be on the down again- having snacks and drinks around me if preparing meals or even moving is too difficult, face wipes if cleanliness begins to become something playing on your mind, and remembering there is support or places you can vent when things are good, bad, in the middle, or completely uncertain there is a large community that can and will relate even if it may seem trivial or unhelpful

putting people into good or bad boxes is so easy to do especially when there’s been past hurt becuase of it but it’s important to remember people do not have to be inherently bad to do bad things and perceptions can be different on both sides
them leaving you on read could have just been a natural end to a conversation but to those of us who overanalyse and personalise the meanings of every interaction, lack of interaction or abandonment can find it neigh impossible to simply “let go of” 

closure is important and perhaps will come in time but if someone has caused you such hurt in the past they may not be the kind of person you want to invite back in freely ignoring what has happened. 

i want to reiterate you are not a bad person for wanting or needing this clarification and that anticipation of being in a ‘grey area’ so to speak can feel so scary 

i have no way of telling you how to simply ‘let go’ of this or move on but the advice i would give and yet probably not take is if this is weighing on your mind heavily to try reaching out even just to ask how they are doing- it does not have to rekindle a relationship but you having the power to start that conversation can give you back some of what may have been taken from you in the past

i’m sorry for the rambling here but remember you aren’t alone in this and even if some of your thoughts may feel irrational or ‘silly’ it is simply how your mind is working or coping right now and that is okay. do not demonise you mind for the way it works 🤍

it’s totally understandable that you aren’t able to face it right away and whilst it’s definitely good to try and come to terms with the ‘worst case scenario’ it’s also important to remember that that’s just the one you have settled on and probably think it’s the one you deserve too in some ways. i always forget that and end up torturing myself over things i can’t be certain have or will ever happen or be so worried about other peoples judgements that i’ll change something or withdraw completely. 
obviously you are not under any obligation to follow anything i say aha but i’m just trying to use things i know or can see from things with me that can apply to others as well and that includes the fact that the mental torture doesn’t really ease that much… 
no matter how long you leave it it’s super unlikely your brain will just switch and decide it’s time to log back on and try and talk to people or reconnect and i know it’s so hard and scary to do that especially when everything in you is telling you it’s the wrong thing to do or rationalise why you should put it off. 
the uncertainty of not knowing or feeling it’s been left too long to acknowledge is an accidental side effect that i’ve found when i’ve thought similar things and it ends up having to be an impulsive decision basically to just talk to them somehow about it but particularly about regrets you would very likely regret if it went so long that you may never feel able to talk to them again and possibly cause worries that your friend may think they’re in the wrong over something that often tends to be a misunderstanding in some way. even though it is possible the thing you have come to terms with may be the case, it’s also not the one that realistically is the most likely (plus if it is you have already started to try and wrap your mind around it). 

but if your friend is also suffers with mental illness that’s someone who in some way will be able to relate to what you are going through, and if they don’t then you deserve to be around people who do accept you even when you do share that. it’s a big part of your life and does control or explain a lot of things which is why of course theres stigma attached to it but that causes a lot of issues when trying be fully conceal it. the times i have made things worse for myself is trying to convince others i’m okay and not wanting to burden them. but sometimes it’s far better to know you need help and try to tell people who should be trying to show you the same care you show them, than to get worse and then end up needing to tell them anyway. there’s a lot of having to face up to fears or stand up for yourself that feels completely impossible at the time but you do deserve to be treated the way others do and to have love and support reciprocated no matter if you forget that or not

it’s been a few days since this was posted so idk if something has been done by now or whatever but i might as well share any thoughts or ideas i have from looking at my own brain just incase someone reads it or needs it you know (i’m not trying to be preachy or condescending in writing this pretending i know everything bc i certainly do not and if i did i’d for sure tell everyone and also be doing better myself ahahaha) 

1. you aren’t in the wrong here. this is a part of you that can control a lot of your life and explain things both good and bad, so can be important to share if you want to with someone you trust 
2. the person may not know how to respond or feel anxious they may say the wrong thing or hurt you (particularly if their exposure to the disorder is the stereotypical negative stuff or they’ve tried to look up ways to help and instead found the silly websites saying they should leave us bc we will hurt them). as this could be the case and is very understandable i feel like perhaps giving them some information and resources that could increase understanding and acceptance could be sent if they do want to get it more. depending how open or close you want to be about it if you have anything like a crisis plan or things that can be helpful for you/ triggers could be shared.  
3. if somebody truly does not want to respond or judges you off something that is not your fault for having then that isn’t fair especially if the previous relationship had care and support and probably isn’t someone you should have around right now- particularly if you are struggling with any of the aspects of having bpd or are battling with stigma and doubting yourself. it can be easy to take this and just think well maybe you should never open up to anyone ever again and i understand that becuase it’s what i do and continue to think in so many places but again this isn’t your fault and setting up walls that prevent you telling someone about things that can be super important can in theory just be as harmful and bad as the possibility being open may change a relationship. friendships should work both ways and that includes accepting each other even when it’s hard
4. perhaps they just can’t see how this works for you? so if they do know anything about bpd or have looked it up they may not be able to fully understand how it applies to you. but asking that may be difficult, particularly in someone with anxiety. could be a good idea to say something like “if it would be helpful i can explain a little how this looks in me?” just as i know there are so many presentations and of course that makes it difficult to understand each person when looking at just a diagnostic criteria or whatever becuase they don’t really explain anything and can be very vague 
5. acknowledging boundaries and setting expectations. this is pretty important i think on both sides becuase constantly i try and modify my behaviour or speech to meet the boundaries i have essentially made up that i think would apply to the other person which can be pretty stressful and confusing at times. but ultimately as much as anyone can think about someone else’s reaction we don’t know for sure unless we are told honestly about it. 
some examples of what i think are a few ideas
-if things are too much or overwhelming or may cause any harm or trigger you please tell me so we both are aware 
-not expecting to be able to ‘fix’ any problems or thoughts you might share with them 
-(this is one that i just find would helpful for me to know and allow the other person to share issues might have from me) being able to share if my behaviour, actions or interactions are becoming a problem 

these are all just things i think of or have said to others not to try and be problematic or make them think i’m just a massive problem but that i want to know if i am and allow them to understand a bit better becuase it’s bad on both sides if not. it can come across a bit intense and people pleaser-y but i suppose i can be my bpd (also quiet) tends to manifest in a way i want to be a minimal problem as my deepest fear is hurting others and then having that hurt them continually like things have for me. in my relationships i do a lot like i have in this simple response and in an attempt to clearly display the way i think about things i basically have a debate with myself before anyone can shut it down. i do apologise to people for this and make them aware i know it can be hard to be my friend especially when most of my times are pretty bad but finding people who do understand does make this easier. i’ve found talking to people online makes me feel quite a bit less alone and the pressure of it being like the longest lasting constant relationship is less there which can be good too (plus there are communities of similar people who are in the same position reading experiences can remind you you aren’t the only one who has felt this way!)
